To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the extent to which a complementor firm can sustain its performance superiority depends on the structural and evolutionary characteristics of the business ecosystem in which it operates and (2) the platform firm’s actions and rules, such as the number of subsystems that the complementor’s products interact with and the frequency of platform transitions, can affect the performance sustainability of complementors.

ecosystem complexity helps firms sustain their superior performance in the ecosystem, while platform transitions initiated by the central platform firm make it more difficult to sustain performance superiority.
the performance of complementors in a platform-based ecosystem is shaped by (1) ecosystem complexity and (2) the generational transitions initiated over time by the platform firms.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the performance of a business firm can be sustained in an environment that is complex and dynamic.
the question of how the rules and actions that platform firms set may influence the performance of complementors in the ecosystem.
how the structural and dynamic features of the ecosystem shape the performance of complementors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ecosystem complexity and generational transitions are two key factors affecting the performance of app developers, and the effects of ecosystem complexity are stronger for more experienced app developers.
the ecosystem complexity is a key determinant of the extent to which the complementor firm can sustain its superior performance.
the ecosystem complexity and the generational transitions initiated and managed by platform firms have a significant effect on the ability of app developers to sustain superior performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ecosystem’s structural and evolutionary features can help us understand the performance of complementors, and that this is a function of their experience in the ecosystem.
the performance sustainability of complementors in business ecosystems may depend on both the structural and evolutionary characteristics of the ecosystem.

the performance of app developers in the smartphone ecosystems can be sustained by (a) having a higher number of unique components that interact with the apps, (b) having more experience in the ecosystem, and (c) having the platform firm initiate fewer transitions in the platform.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of complementors in business ecosystems is shaped by the structural and evolutionary characteristics of the ecosystems.
platform firms should be aware of the potential consequences of their rules and actions in terms of the sustainability of the superior performance of complementors.
platform firms should consider the structural and evolutionary characteristics of the business ecosystems they orchestrate in their strategic decision-making.
